challenges.name: dependency-direction-quiz
challenges.title: Which way does this import point?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the orders module: how OrderService gets its repository, and a layer check that found a domain file importing a service.

questions.explanation: False. The service imports the concrete PostgresOrderRepository and the shared db connection, and creates the repository itself, so it depends on Postgres through that import: the unit test fails with ECONNREFUSED because placeOrder cannot run without a real database. Hiding the SQL in another class moves the code, not the dependency. The fix is to depend on an interface the service owns in the domain layer (an OrderRepository port with save()), receive an implementation in the constructor, and let only the composition root (main.ts) create PostgresOrderRepository. The misconception is that a dependency means "contains the SQL": a dependency is anything you import and cannot run without.

True. Today order.ts imports pricingService.ts and pricingService.ts imports order.ts: a cycle, and the domain -> service arrow is the half that points the wrong way. applyDiscount uses nothing from the service layer, so it belongs next to orderTotal in the domain. After the move, the only arrow left is pricingService -> domain, which is allowed, and the check prints 0 violations. Verify it by rerunning the check and with a cycle finder such as madge --circular. The misconception is that a cycle must be broken with an interface or a third shared module; often one function is simply in the wrong layer.

challenges.name: check-dependency-direction
challenges.title: Check the dependency direction
challenges.description: Reviewers of the CodeDev API keep missing imports that point the wrong way between layers. Write the check that CI will run. layerOf(path): split the path on "/", drop the last part (the file name) and take the FIRST remaining folder named "controllers" (layer "controller"), "services" ("service"), "domain" ("domain") or "repositories" ("repository"), compared exactly (case-sensitive). A path with none of them has no layer (null) and is never checked, as importer or as import: shared code, packages such as "zod" or "node:crypto", tests. Allowed imports (importing layer -> imported layer): every layer may import its own layer and the domain; controller -> service is allowed. Forbidden, with the rule to report: controller -> repository is "controller-skips-service"; service -> repository is "service-needs-port" (a service reaches the database only through a port, an interface in the domain layer that a repository implements); service -> controller, repository -> controller and repository -> service are "points-backward"; domain -> controller, service or repository is "domain-must-be-pure". findViolations(files) gets [{ path, imports }] with imports already resolved to paths from the repository root, and returns one { file, import, from, to, rule } per forbidden import (from and to are the two layers). The same import listed twice in one file is reported once. Sort by file, then by import, both A to Z compared with < and >. No violations: an empty array. The test runner reads { files } as JSON from stdin and prints the result as JSON.
hints: Two separate questions decide each import: which layer is each path in, and is that pair of layers allowed? Can you answer the second one with a lookup instead of a chain of if statements?

Look at layerOf first: the file name must not count (src/orders/services.ts has no layer), and the first matching folder wins (src/orders/domain/services/pricing.ts is domain). Then write the 4 x 4 table from the description as a nested object where an allowed cell is null and a forbidden cell holds the rule name, and remove repeated imports of one file before you check them.

A similar check on another tree: the layers are "pages" -> "page" and "api" -> "api", and only api -> page is forbidden (rule "api-imports-ui"). For app/blog/pages/post.tsx, layerOf gives "page"; for app/blog/api/pages/list.ts it gives "api" (the first matching folder), and for app/blog/pages.ts it gives null. The file app/blog/api/pages/list.ts importing app/blog/pages/post.tsx twice gives one entry: { file: "app/blog/api/pages/list.ts", import: "app/blog/pages/post.tsx", from: "api", to: "page", rule: "api-imports-ui" }.

tests.name: The orders module: a controller reads the repository, a service skips the port
Backward imports: domain to service and controller, repository and service to the layer above
The first matching folder decides; a file named services.ts or a Services folder has no layer
Every allowed direction passes: same layer, inward imports and ports
A repeated import is reported once; sorted by file, then by import
Paths outside any layer are not checked: packages, shared code, tests, a folder import
Large codebase: about 200 files across five modules and four layers
